_about: Editorial summaries shown on each state page. Tokens such as {rank:vcrime} and {v:gdp} are resolved against the current data at build time — see scripts/lib/notes.mjs.
AK: No individual income tax and no statewide sales tax; the {rank:burden} state-local tax burden in the country ({v:burden} of income), funded largely by petroleum revenue.
AL: Auto assembly (Mercedes, Honda, Hyundai, Mazda-Toyota) and aerospace in Huntsville anchor a manufacturing-heavy economy.
AR: Home to Walmart, Tyson Foods and J.B. Hunt; retail and distribution give a small state outsized corporate weight.
AZ: A 2.5% flat income tax — the lowest flat rate in the nation — alongside a major semiconductor build-out led by TSMC and Intel in metro Phoenix.
CA: The {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy ({v:gdp}) and, on its own, among the five largest economies in the world. The {rank:itaxTop} top marginal income tax rate ({v:itaxTop}) and the {rank:gasTax} state gas tax.
CO: Lowest state sales tax rate among states that levy one (2.9%), but the third-highest average local add-on (4.99%).
CT: The {rank:burden} state-local tax burden in the nation; insurance in Hartford and defense manufacturing (submarines, jet engines) dominate output.
DC: The {rank:gdpPerCapita} GDP per capita and the {rank:ba} bachelor's-degree share in the country; federal government activity dominates output, so growth tracks federal budgets.
DE: No sales tax; the legal home of most large US corporations, which makes corporate franchise fees a major revenue source.
FL: {Rank:growth:fastest/slowest} real GDP growth of any state in 2025 ({v:growth}). No income tax, and a constitutional amendment lifts the minimum wage to $15 in late 2026.
GA: Converted from graduated to a flat income tax in 2024 and is stepping the rate down; the Port of Savannah and Hartsfield-Jackson make it a national logistics hub.
HI: The {rank:propTax} effective property tax rate in the nation ({v:propTax}), paired with the {rank:col} cost of living and the {rank:lifeExp:longest/shortest} life expectancy.
IA: Collapsed a nine-bracket income tax into a single 3.8% flat rate in 2025 — one of the fastest tax overhauls of the decade.
ID: The {rank:popChg:fastest-growing/fastest-shrinking} state population since 2020 ({v:popChg}), which has put sustained pressure on housing costs.
IL: The {rank:propTax} effective property tax rate ({v:propTax}) and the {rank:gasTax} state gas tax; Chicago is the rail and futures-trading hub of the country.
IN: The most manufacturing-intensive large state economy — roughly a quarter of output — and on a legislated path to a 2.9% flat income tax.
KS: Wichita builds much of the world's general-aviation fleet; the state fully exempted groceries from sales tax in 2025.
KY: Ratcheting its flat income tax down toward 3.0% under a revenue-trigger law; Louisville's UPS hub makes it a top air-cargo state.
LA: The {rank:salesCombined} combined sales tax rate in the nation ({v:salesCombined}) after a 2025 overhaul that traded a flat 3% income tax for a higher state sales tax.
MA: The {rank:mhi@states} median household income of any state ({v:mhi}) and the {rank:uninsured} uninsured rate ({v:uninsured}). A 2023 surtax adds 4 points above $1M of income, giving a 9% top rate.
MD: The {rank:mhi@states} median household income of any state ({v:mhi}); NIH, NSA and Johns Hopkins concentrate federal research spending here.
ME: The {rank:vcrime} violent crime rate in the country ({v:vcrime} per 100,000) and the oldest median age of any state.
MI: The centre of US auto engineering; output growth has lagged as the industry's EV transition shifted capital investment to the South.
MN: The {rank:lifeExp:longest/shortest} life expectancy in the country; the Mayo Clinic and medtech cluster drive high-wage employment.
MO: Lowest state sales tax rate among states with a general sales tax outside Colorado (4.225%), offset by high local add-ons.
MS: The {rank:mhi} median household income ({v:mhi}) and the {rank:lifeExp:longest/shortest} life expectancy ({v:lifeExp} years) in the country; legislated to phase its flat income tax toward zero.
MT: No sales tax of any kind, and cutting its top income tax rate from 5.9% to 5.65% in 2026 with a further cut to 5.4% legislated for 2027.
NC: The lowest corporate income tax rate among states that levy one, legislated to reach zero by 2030; Charlotte is the second-largest US banking centre.
ND: The {rank:unemp} unemployment rate ({v:unemp}) and the highest per-capita oil output; Bakken production makes GDP unusually sensitive to crude prices.
NE: The {rank:lfpr@states} labour force participation of any state ({v:lfpr}); cutting both individual and corporate top rates toward 3.99% by 2027.
NH: The {rank:poverty} poverty rate in the nation ({v:poverty}) and the {rank:vcrime} violent crime rate. No income tax and no sales tax, but the {rank:propTax} property tax rate pays for it.
NJ: The {rank:corpTax} corporate income tax rate ({v:corpTax}) and the {rank:propTax} property tax rate, alongside low crime and high incomes.
NM: The {rank:vcrime} violent crime rate ({v:vcrime} per 100,000); Permian Basin production has made it the second-largest oil-producing state and filled its sovereign-style permanent funds.
NV: No individual or corporate income tax (a gross-receipts commerce tax applies instead); the most tourism-dependent state economy in the nation.
NY: The {rank:burden} state-local tax burden in the nation ({v:burden} of income) and the {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy; real growth of {v:growth} in 2025 was the {rank:growth:fastest/slowest}.
OH: The {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy ({v:gdp}). No corporate income tax (a commercial activity tax applies instead) and moving to a 2.75% flat individual rate in 2026.
OK: Collapsed six income tax brackets into three and cut its top rate from 4.75% to 4.5% effective January 2026.
OR: No sales tax but a 9.9% top income tax rate; Intel's largest global R&D site makes semiconductors the dominant export.
PA: The {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy ({v:gdp}) and the second-largest natural gas producer; its corporate rate is stepping down from 9.99% in 2022 to 4.99% by 2031.
RI: The smallest state by area; its economy is tightly integrated with Boston's labour market and the Navy's undersea warfare centre.
SC: {Rank:growth:fastest/slowest} real GDP growth of any state in 2025 ({v:growth}) and the {rank:popChg:fastest-growing/fastest-shrinking} population since 2020; BMW and Boeing anchor export manufacturing.
SD: The {rank:unemp} unemployment rate in the country ({v:unemp}). No individual or corporate income tax, which drew the national credit-card industry to Sioux Falls.
TN: The {rank:burden} tax burden ({v:burden}) with no income tax, but the {rank:salesCombined} combined sales tax rate ({v:salesCombined}).
TX: The {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy and the largest oil producer. No income tax, funded by high property and sales taxes; the {rank:uninsured} uninsured rate in the nation ({v:uninsured}).
UT: The {rank:poverty} poverty rate and the youngest median age in the country; real growth of {v:growth} in 2025 was the {rank:growth:fastest/slowest}.
VA: Northern Virginia carries the largest concentration of data centres on earth — roughly a third of global cloud capacity routes through Loudoun County.
VT: The {rank:gdp:largest/smallest} state economy ({v:gdp}) and the {rank:unemp} unemployment rate; the {rank:propTax} property tax rate funds a statewide education system.
WA: No tax on wage income but a 7% tax on capital gains above a threshold, no corporate income tax (a gross-receipts B&O tax applies), and the {rank:minWage@states} state minimum wage.
WI: The most dairy-intensive state economy and a top-five manufacturing share of output; large 2024-25 income tax cuts targeted the middle brackets.
WV: The {rank:ownRate} homeownership rate ({v:ownRate}) and the {rank:homeValue} median home value; the {rank:ba} bachelor's-degree share and the {rank:lfpr} labour force participation.
WY: The {rank:burden} tax burden ({v:burden}) and the {rank:pop:largest/smallest} population; mineral extraction is roughly a fifth of state output, the highest share in the nation.
